key_insight: KATOsuper speeds topology optimization by using a sensitivity-consistent Fourier neural operator so the predicted objective and its gradient stay aligned during optimization.
engineering_relevance: It enables much faster, resolution-invariant design optimization for 2D and 3D compliance/stress problems, making surrogate-assisted topology optimization more practical for real engineering workflows.
method: Neural-reparameterized topology optimization with an objective-agnostic SC-FNO surrogate
Forward_split architecture: compute sensitivities by automatic differentiation through the predicted objective field
Physics-informed multi-channel encoding with Fourier position embedding; 3D extension via KATO3D with KANConv3D blocks
evidence_signal: Evaluated on three 2D benchmarks and three 3D structures, showing 15–110x deployment-time speedup over MATLAB baselines while remaining competitive in optimality.
watch_item: Zero-shot extrapolation is promising but performance still depends on how well approximate surrogate gradients preserve the true sensitivity direction, especially at large scaling factors or in complex 3D cases.
paper_title: KATOsuper: Surrogate-accelerated neural topology optimization with sensitivity-consistent Fourier neural operators
